summary: Lolo National Forest L-4 tower in Mineral County, built 1936 and destroyed in 1965; named lookouts from 1948 to 1954; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 50-foot round timber pole tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1965 per both accounts; no source describes remains at the site

events.note: 50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (firelookout.com); round timber tower with L-4 cab (Forest Lookouts)
Fern Bonnell, a St. Regis school teacher, took over the summer lookout duties (Mineral Independent item, July 1948, quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Wally "Bigfoot" Hahn, named as a lookout by firelookout.com
Mack Mage, named as a lookout by firelookout.com
Jim Bookie, named as a lookout by firelookout.com

evidence.supports: about 1.5 miles east of an earlier point two miles NNE of Sheep Mountain
evidence.quote: 1.5 miles east of first point 2 miles NNE of Sheep Mtn.

evidence.supports: built 1936; round timber tower with L-4 cab
evidence.quote: 1936: A round timber tower with an L-4 cab was erected.

evidence.supports: Fern Bonnell took over summer lookout duties, July 1948
evidence.quote: Miss Fern Bonnell, St. Regis school teacher, assumed summer duties, as lookout at the Marble Point station between Superior and St. Regis, last week.

evidence.supports: had worked the station for the three summers before
evidence.quote: Miss Bonnel has been a forest service lookout on this station for the last three summers.
Known lookout personnel: 1950: Wally "Bigfoot" Hahn; 1953: Mack Mage; 1954: Jim Bookie.

notes_for_editor: Both pages agree on 1936 and 1965. The named lookouts (1950, 1953, 1954) come from firelookout.com alone, and the 1948 item is quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts; the original Mineral Independent was not read. The Montana/Idaho fire lookout NRHP form (MT_ID_FireLookoutsMPD.pdf) was searched for Marble Point and returned no matching text. No source read describes the site today or its access.
